findings.description: Inconsistent use of `storage_route.alias`. Files still reference `storage_route.token` instead of `storage_route.alias`.
CRLF stripping to HTTP 400 rejection is not explicitly mandated across all files. PR.md omits it entirely, and philosophy.md mentions rejection without explicitly enforcing the HTTP 400 response.
Vendor neutrality is violated. Files contain forbidden references to S3, GCS, AWS (s3.amazonaws.com), React, and V8.
The redundant distributed lock (SETNX) abstraction has not been fully removed. Section 1.1 explicitly praises the 'transient SETNX lock'.

residual_risks: Incomplete transition of terminology (`token` vs `alias`) could lead to diverging implementations in SDKs.
Vendor-specific logic might accidentally couple architecture implementations if the documentation implicitly allows it.
testing_gaps: Verify that integration tests assert HTTP 400 strictly on CRLF injection without relying on implicit behavior.
